2	  "argument_markdown": "## 0. Scope, conventions, and excluded routes\n\nWork throughout with Q-coefficients. Geometry is that of ATT-0112 (C66-GEO-COMP; dual-confirmed by REV-0157 and REV-0158) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, after base change to C so that Betti mixed Hodge structures are defined. Write X := M_{6,6} for the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack of smooth genus-six curves with six ordered marked points, of dimension d = 21. The target\n\nT := W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(X; Q)\n\nis identified with W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q)(21) by Poincar\u00e9 duality (established working-context fact; packet FND-0001). In particular H^{26}(X; Q) is mixed of weights at least 26, so W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) = Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) is a pure polarizable Hodge structure of weight 26, and T is pure of weight -16. Borel-Moore homology is dual to compactly supported cohomology in the same degree with no extra Tate twist (established fact). Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, so Gr^W_m is an exact functor.\n\nThe mixed Hodge theory used below is exactly the Q-coefficient theory already employed to name T on the smooth stack X and on its open substacks: ordinary cohomology of a smooth finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack, and the restriction map along an open immersion of such stacks. Compactly supported cohomology of a possibly singular closed substack is not used as a standalone input.\n\nCasnati-Ekedahl conventions, (CE)+(N)+(BAL), H = H_{4,6}(P^1), and H^bal = {F isomorphic to O(4)+O(5)} are as in ATT-0112. No global splitting W = W_4 + W_5 is used. No blocked route is used. In particular this argument never invokes vcd-only vanishing, the undecorated top-weight graph complex, a point count, or the forgetful map X -> M_{6,5}. Gysin maps, a closed embedding of the reduced-support model itself into X, support-exhaustion, and a monomorphism f: Z -> X are not assumed; the only map to T that is used is constructed in Section 5 from restriction of ordinary cohomology.\n\n## 1. Source geometry (imported from ATT-0112)\n\nBy ATT-0112/CLM-0112-1 and CLM-0112-2, H is a finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack, smooth of pure dimension 18, and H^bal is open in H, hence itself smooth of pure dimension 18, reduced and normal. By ATT-0112/CLM-0112-6 and CLM-0112-7, every nonempty connected component of H^bal (and of Hbar^bal = [H^bal/PGL_2], smooth of pure dimension 15) contains a type-(i) point.\n\nLet V be a finite-type k-scheme with a smooth surjective morphism V -> H^bal (a smooth atlas; H^bal of finite type supplies a finite-type atlas). Let V_beta be any connected component. ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8, over this reduced locally Noetherian scheme, supplies:\n\n- pi_* L locally free of rank three and AJ = P_{V_beta}(pi_* L) a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle;\n- U_beta the distinct-support (reduced-support) open of AJ, V_beta-smooth of pure relative dimension two and surjective;\n- Z_beta = Ord(U_beta) -> U_beta the finite \u00e9tale right S_6-torsor of orderings of the universal degree-six divisor, of degree 720;\n- Z_beta equal to the CE evaluation-failure model (via the dual-confirmed identifications recorded in ATT-0112 clause (E): ATT-0065/CLM-0065-9 and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-5, CLM-0066-6).\n\nIn particular Z_beta is a smooth finite-type k-scheme. The reduced-support condition and the ordering are applied to the same scheme; no one-sided reduction is used. Grauert is used only over the reduced scheme V_beta.\n\nWrite Z for the disjoint union of the Z_beta as V_beta runs over connected components of a chosen atlas, or equivalently for any single Z_beta when only geometric points of the image are at issue. Nothing below uses a component formula over a stack with inertia (FND-0144).\n\n## 2. The classifying morphism (constructed, not assumed)\n\nOver Z_beta the pullback of the universal curve of AJ is a smooth proper family C_{Z_beta} -> Z_beta of geometrically connected genus-six curves, equipped with six tautological pairwise-disjoint sections sigma_1, ..., sigma_6 whose relative Cartier divisor is the universal reduced member of |L|. This is precisely an object of the fibre category X(Z_beta). By the 2-Yoneda description of the moduli stack, this object is a morphism of locally finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks\n\nf_beta : Z_beta -> X = M_{6,6}.\n\nNo comparison of Aut(C, gamma, Gamma) with Aut(C, Gamma) is used: existence of f_beta is the universal property of X, which classifies marked curves and does not see the pencil. No claim that f_beta is a monomorphism, unramified, quasi-finite, representable in any stronger sense than a morphism from a scheme to a Deligne-Mumford stack, or a closed immersion, is made. (The blocked monomorphism-without-pencil-recovery route is therefore not taken; pencil recovery is not needed for existence.)\n\nGeometrically, a geometric point of the image is an ordered six-pointed smooth genus-six curve (C, p_1, ..., p_6) for which the p_i are pairwise distinct and O_C(p_1+...+p_6) is isomorphic to L on a balanced tetragonal cover (C, gamma) presenting that point of H^bal. This is a description of geometric points of the image, not a stack-level full-faithfulness statement.\n\n## 3. Atlas-independent closed support Y\n\nThe morphism f_beta is of finite type (source and target are). The set-theoretic image of a finite-type morphism of algebraic stacks locally of finite type over a field is a constructible subset of the Zariski topological space of geometric points (Chevalley for algebraic stacks). Let Im be the union of the geometric images of all f_beta for the connected components of a fixed atlas. Let |Y| be the Zariski closure of Im in |X|, and let Y be the unique reduced closed substack of X with underlying space |Y|. The closed immersion i: Y -> X exists by this definition of Y; it is not a closed embedding of Z_beta, and it is not asserted to be a regular immersion, lci, or of pure codimension four.\n\nAtlas independence. Let V -> H^bal and V' -> H^bal be two smooth finite-type atlases, with associated images Im and Im'. The fibre product W = V times_{H^bal} V' is again a smooth atlas, and the tautological families on Z_W pull back from both sides, so the classifying morphisms commute with the projections Z_W -> Z_V and Z_W -> Z_{V'}. Smooth (in particular, surjective on geometric points) pullback therefore yields Im = Im_W = Im'. Equivalently, a geometric point of H^bal is an isomorphism class of (C, gamma), and a geometric point of Z is an ordering of a reduced member of |L|; both are intrinsic to the moduli problem and independent of presentation. Hence Y, as the reduced closure of that intrinsic set of geometric points of X, is independent of the atlas.\n\nThe same Y is obtained if one starts from an \u00e9tale atlas of Hbar^bal = [H^bal / PGL_2]: precomposition of gamma with an automorphism of the target replaces D by a linearly equivalent divisor in the same pencil, so (C, Gamma) in X is PGL_2-invariant (ATT-0112/CLM-0112-7). The geometric image in X is therefore unchanged.\n\nY is nonempty: H^bal is nonempty (imported in ATT-0112 from FND-0154), and on every balanced geometric fibre the reduced-support open is nonempty (ATT-0112 clause (E) via ATT-0088/CLM-0088-5, CLM-0088-8). Nonemptiness of Y is recorded only to make the construction non-vacuous; vanishing of T_Z is not excluded and is not needed.\n\n## 4. Localization sequence for X along Y\n\nLet U_Y := X \\ Y, an open substack of the smooth stack X, hence itself smooth of dimension 21. Open-closed decomposition supplies the localization triangle in the derived category of mixed Hodge complexes on the analytic site of X,\n\nR Gamma_Y(X, Q) -> R Gamma(X, Q) -> R Gamma(U_Y, Q) -> +1,\n\nor equivalently the long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures whose degree-26 fragment contains the restriction morphism of ordinary cohomology\n\nr : H^{26}(X; Q) -> H^{26}(U_Y; Q).\n\nThis is a localization sequence for X = M_{6,6}, constructed from the closed-open pair (Y, U_Y). Both X and U_Y are smooth of dimension 21, so H^{26}(X; Q) and H^{26}(U_Y; Q) have weights at least 26, and W_{26} = Gr^W_{26} on each. Strictness yields that\n\nGr^W_{26} r : Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) -> Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)\n\nis a morphism of pure polarizable Hodge structures of weight 26. Twisting by (21) and applying the Poincar\u00e9 identification of T gives a morphism of pure weight -16 Hodge structures\n\nr_T : T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21).\n\nNo Gysin morphism, no fundamental class of Y, and no degree shift by twice the codimension appear. The map r_T is restriction of ordinary cohomology, which exists for an arbitrary open immersion of smooth stacks and does not require Y to be regularly immersed.\n\n(If one prefers the language of cohomology with supports, ker(r) = im(H^{26}_Y(X; Q) -> H^{26}(X; Q)), so the kernel constructed below is exactly the image of the supports map in the sense of FND-0168(3a), once the closed support Y containing the image of Z has been fixed. The kernel itself is named without treating H_c^*(Y) as a standalone theory.)\n\n## 5. The datum (K_Z, T_Z, phi)\n\nDefine\n\nK_Z := ker(r_T) = ker( T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21) ),\n\nT_Z := K_Z,\n\nphi : K_Z -> T the inclusion of this kernel.\n\nThen:\n\n- K_Z is a named mixed Hodge structure: it is the kernel of W_{26} of restriction in the localization sequence of Section 4 for M_{6,6}. Equivalently it is W_{26} of the degree-26 supports group H^{26}_Y(X; Q), twisted by (21). Degree, weight, and twist are those of T: Borel-Moore degree 16, weight -16, ordinary cohomological degree 26 with Poincar\u00e9 twist (21). No Tate type is asserted.\n- phi is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures, constructed as W_{26}(21) of the restriction map r of Section 4 (or as the supports-to-ambient map). It is not assumed; it is this restriction/kernel inclusion.\n- T_Z is the kernel of r_T, hence a subobject of T, hence a specified subquotient of T. Exactness of Gr^W_{26} on the localization sequence at H^{26}(X) says precisely that T_Z consists of those classes in T whose restriction to U_Y vanishes in W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21).\n\nThis is the CE support-accounting datum attached to the ordered reduced-support evaluation-failure geometry, via the closed support Y constructed from that geometry in Sections 2-3.\n\n## 6. Coverage: no relevant Z-supported term is omitted\n\nBy construction of Y, every geometric point of the image of f_beta lies in Y, so the image of Z is contained in Y and U_Y is disjoint from that image. Any class in T that is supported on a closed subset of X contained in Y (in particular, any class supported on the closure of the image of Z, and any class supported on the image of Z itself) restricts to zero on U_Y, hence lies in ker(r_T) = T_Z.\n\nThus every Z-supported corner class in T, in the only sense available before a regular embedding is proved \u2014 namely, a class in T that vanishes on the complement of a closed support containing the image of Z \u2014 is accounted for in T_Z. The identification is exact at T: T_Z = ker(r_T), so the complementary term in the localization sequence is the image of T in W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21), which is a subobject of the corner of the open complement and is excluded from T_Z by definition.\n\nCoverage is one-sided on purpose. The kernel may include classes supported on extra components of the closure Y (non-reduced members of |L| in the fibrewise discriminant, and any unbalanced or boundary points that happen to lie in the closure). Including extra support does not omit a Z-supported term. Support-exhaustion T_Z = T is not claimed: that would require vanishing or Tate-ness of the complementary corner, which is a C66-TATE-ASSEMBLY input, not this interface.\n\nUnbalanced Casnati-Ekedahl strata that do not meet Y are not part of the ordered reduced-support balanced geometry of ATT-0112 clause (E); they are complementary target terms, not omitted Z-terms of this datum.\n\n## 7. Descent and atlas invariance\n\nK_Z, T_Z, and phi are defined from the pair (X, Y) alone. Section 3 shows that Y is the reduced closure of an atlas-independent set of geometric points of X. Therefore any two presentations \u2014 any two smooth finite-type scheme atlases of H^bal, any \u00e9tale atlas of Hbar^bal, and the stacky incidence over H^bal itself \u2014 produce the same closed substack Y and the same datum (K_Z, T_Z, phi).   "argument_markdown": "## 0. Scope, conventions, and excluded routes\n\nWork throughout with Q-coefficients. Geometry is that of ATT-0112 (C66-GEO-COMP; dual-confirmed by REV-0157 and REV-0158) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, after base change to C so that Betti mixed Hodge structures are defined. Write X := M_{6,6} for the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack of smooth genus-six curves with six ordered marked points, of dimension d = 21. The target\n\nT := W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(X; Q)\n\nis identified with W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q)(21) by Poincar\u00e9 duality (established working-context fact; packet FND-0001). In particular H^{26}(X; Q) is mixed of weights at least 26, so W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) = Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) is a pure polarizable Hodge structure of weight 26, and T is pure of weight -16. Borel-Moore homology is dual to compactly supported cohomology in the same degree with no extra Tate twist (established fact). Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, so Gr^W_m is an exact functor.\n\nThe mixed Hodge theory used below is exactly the Q-coefficient theory already employed to name T on the smooth stack X and on its open substacks: ordinary cohomology of a smooth finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack, and the restriction map along an open immersion of such stacks. Compactly supported cohomology of a possibly singular closed substack is not used as a standalone input.\n\nCasnati-Ekedahl conventions, (CE)+(N)+(BAL), H = H_{4,6}(P^1), and H^bal = {F isomorphic to O(4)+O(5)} are as in ATT-0112. No global splitting W = W_4 + W_5 is used. No blocked route is used. In particular this argument never invokes vcd-only vanishing, the undecorated top-weight graph complex, a point count, or the forgetful map X -> M_{6,5}. Gysin maps, a closed embedding of the reduced-support model itself into X, support-exhaustion, and a monomorphism f: Z -> X are not assumed; the only map to T that is used is constructed in Section 5 from restriction of ordinary cohomology.\n\n## 1. Source geometry (imported from ATT-0112)\n\nBy ATT-0112/CLM-0112-1 and CLM-0112-2, H is a finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack, smooth of pure dimension 18, and H^bal is open in H, hence itself smooth of pure dimension 18, reduced and normal. By ATT-0112/CLM-0112-6 and CLM-0112-7, every nonempty connected component of H^bal (and of Hbar^bal = [H^bal/PGL_2], smooth of pure dimension 15) contains a type-(i) point.\n\nLet V be a finite-type k-scheme with a smooth surjective morphism V -> H^bal (a smooth atlas; H^bal of finite type supplies a finite-type atlas). Let V_beta be any connected component. ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8, over this reduced locally Noetherian scheme, supplies:\n\n- pi_* L locally free of rank three and AJ = P_{V_beta}(pi_* L) a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle;\n- U_beta the distinct-support (reduced-support) open of AJ, V_beta-smooth of pure relative dimension two and surjective;\n- Z_beta = Ord(U_beta) -> U_beta the finite \u00e9tale right S_6-torsor of orderings of the universal degree-six divisor, of degree 720;\n- Z_beta equal to the CE evaluation-failure model (via the dual-confirmed identifications recorded in ATT-0112 clause (E): ATT-0065/CLM-0065-9 and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-5, CLM-0066-6).\n\nIn particular Z_beta is a smooth finite-type k-scheme. The reduced-support condition and the ordering are applied to the same scheme; no one-sided reduction is used. Grauert is used only over the reduced scheme V_beta.\n\nWrite Z for the disjoint union of the Z_beta as V_beta runs over connected components of a chosen atlas, or equivalently for any single Z_beta when only geometric points of the image are at issue. Nothing below uses a component formula over a stack with inertia (FND-0144).\n\n## 2. The classifying morphism (constructed, not assumed)\n\nOver Z_beta the pullback of the universal curve of AJ is a smooth proper family C_{Z_beta} -> Z_beta of geometrically connected genus-six curves, equipped with six tautological pairwise-disjoint sections sigma_1, ..., sigma_6 whose relative Cartier divisor is the universal reduced member of |L|. This is precisely an object of the fibre category X(Z_beta). By the 2-Yoneda description of the moduli stack, this object is a morphism of locally finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks\n\nf_beta : Z_beta -> X = M_{6,6}.\n\nNo comparison of Aut(C, gamma, Gamma) with Aut(C, Gamma) is used: existence of f_beta is the universal property of X, which classifies marked curves and does not see the pencil. No claim that f_beta is a monomorphism, unramified, quasi-finite, representable in any stronger sense than a morphism from a scheme to a Deligne-Mumford stack, or a closed immersion, is made. (The blocked monomorphism-without-pencil-recovery route is therefore not taken; pencil recovery is not needed for existence.)\n\nGeometrically, a geometric point of the image is an ordered six-pointed smooth genus-six curve (C, p_1, ..., p_6) for which the p_i are pairwise distinct and O_C(p_1+...+p_6) is isomorphic to L on a balanced tetragonal cover (C, gamma) presenting that point of H^bal. This is a description of geometric points of the image, not a stack-level full-faithfulness statement.\n\n## 3. Atlas-independent closed support Y\n\nThe morphism f_beta is of finite type (source and target are). The set-theoretic image of a finite-type morphism of algebraic stacks locally of finite type over a field is a constructible subset of the Zariski topological space of geometric points (Chevalley for algebraic stacks). Let Im be the union of the geometric images of all f_beta for the connected components of a fixed atlas. Let |Y| be the Zariski closure of Im in |X|, and let Y be the unique reduced closed substack of X with underlying space |Y|. The closed immersion i: Y -> X exists by this definition of Y; it is not a closed embedding of Z_beta, and it is not asserted to be a regular immersion, lci, or of pure codimension four.\n\nAtlas independence. Let V -> H^bal and V' -> H^bal be two smooth finite-type atlases, with associated images Im and Im'. The fibre product W = V times_{H^bal} V' is again a smooth atlas, and the tautological families on Z_W pull back from both sides, so the classifying morphisms commute with the projections Z_W -> Z_V and Z_W -> Z_{V'}. Smooth (in particular, surjective on geometric points) pullback therefore yields Im = Im_W = Im'. Equivalently, a geometric point of H^bal is an isomorphism class of (C, gamma), and a geometric point of Z is an ordering of a reduced member of |L|; both are intrinsic to the moduli problem and independent of presentation. Hence Y, as the reduced closure of that intrinsic set of geometric points of X, is independent of the atlas.\n\nThe same Y is obtained if one starts from an \u00e9tale atlas of Hbar^bal = [H^bal / PGL_2]: precomposition of gamma with an automorphism of the target replaces D by a linearly equivalent divisor in the same pencil, so (C, Gamma) in X is PGL_2-invariant (ATT-0112/CLM-0112-7). The geometric image in X is therefore unchanged.\n\nY is nonempty: H^bal is nonempty (imported in ATT-0112 from FND-0154), and on every balanced geometric fibre the reduced-support open is nonempty (ATT-0112 clause (E) via ATT-0088/CLM-0088-5, CLM-0088-8). Nonemptiness of Y is recorded only to make the construction non-vacuous; vanishing of T_Z is not excluded and is not needed.\n\n## 4. Localization sequence for X along Y\n\nLet U_Y := X \\ Y, an open substack of the smooth stack X, hence itself smooth of dimension 21. Open-closed decomposition supplies the localization triangle in the derived category of mixed Hodge complexes on the analytic site of X,\n\nR Gamma_Y(X, Q) -> R Gamma(X, Q) -> R Gamma(U_Y, Q) -> +1,\n\nor equivalently the long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures whose degree-26 fragment contains the restriction morphism of ordinary cohomology\n\nr : H^{26}(X; Q) -> H^{26}(U_Y; Q).\n\nThis is a localization sequence for X = M_{6,6}, constructed from the closed-open pair (Y, U_Y). Both X and U_Y are smooth of dimension 21, so H^{26}(X; Q) and H^{26}(U_Y; Q) have weights at least 26, and W_{26} = Gr^W_{26} on each. Strictness yields that\n\nGr^W_{26} r : Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) -> Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)\n\nis a morphism of pure polarizable Hodge structures of weight 26. Twisting by (21) and applying the Poincar\u00e9 identification of T gives a morphism of pure weight -16 Hodge structures\n\nr_T : T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21).\n\nNo Gysin morphism, no fundamental class of Y, and no degree shift by twice the codimension appear. The map r_T is restriction of ordinary cohomology, which exists for an arbitrary open immersion of smooth stacks and does not require Y to be regularly immersed.\n\n(If one prefers the language of cohomology with supports, ker(r) = im(H^{26}_Y(X; Q) -> H^{26}(X; Q)), so the kernel constructed below is exactly the image of the supports map in the sense of FND-0168(3a), once the closed support Y containing the image of Z has been fixed. The kernel itself is named without treating H_c^*(Y) as a standalone theory.)\n\n## 5. The datum (K_Z, T_Z, phi)\n\nDefine\n\nK_Z := ker(r_T) = ker( T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21) ),\n\nT_Z := K_Z,\n\nphi : K_Z -> T the inclusion of this kernel.\n\nThen:\n\n- K_Z is a named mixed Hodge structure: it is the kernel of W_{26} of restriction in the localization sequence of Section 4 for M_{6,6}. Equivalently it is W_{26} of the degree-26 supports group H^{26}_Y(X; Q), twisted by (21). Degree, weight, and twist are those of T: Borel-Moore degree 16, weight -16, ordinary cohomological degree 26 with Poincar\u00e9 twist (21). No Tate type is asserted.\n- phi is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures, constructed as W_{26}(21) of the restriction map r of Section 4 (or as the supports-to-ambient map). It is not assumed; it is this restriction/kernel inclusion.\n- T_Z is the kernel of r_T, hence a subobject of T, hence a specified subquotient of T. Exactness of Gr^W_{26} on the localization sequence at H^{26}(X) says precisely that T_Z consists of those classes in T whose restriction to U_Y vanishes in W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21).\n\nThis is the CE support-accounting datum attached to the ordered reduced-support evaluation-failure geometry, via the closed support Y constructed from that geometry in Sections 2-3.\n\n## 6. Coverage: no relevant Z-supported term is omitted\n\nBy construction of Y, every geometric point of the image of f_beta lies in Y, so the image of Z is contained in Y and U_Y is disjoint from that image. Any class in T that is supported on a closed subset of X contained in Y (in particular, any class supported on the closure of the image of Z, and any class supported on the image of Z itself) restricts to zero on U_Y, hence lies in ker(r_T) = T_Z.\n\nThus every Z-supported corner class in T, in the only sense available before a regular embedding is proved \u2014 namely, a class in T that vanishes on the complement of a closed support containing the image of Z \u2014 is accounted for in T_Z. The identification is exact at T: T_Z = ker(r_T), so the complementary term in the localization sequence is the image of T in W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21), which is a subobject of the corner of the open complement and is excluded from T_Z by definition.\n\nCoverage is one-sided on purpose. The kernel may include classes supported on extra components of the closure Y (non-reduced members of |L| in the fibrewise discriminant, and any unbalanced or boundary points that happen to lie in the closure). Including extra support does not omit a Z-supported term. Support-exhaustion T_Z = T is not claimed: that would require vanishing or Tate-ness of the complementary corner, which is a C66-TATE-ASSEMBLY input, not this interface.\n\nUnbalanced Casnati-Ekedahl strata that do not meet Y are not part of the ordered reduced-support balanced geometry of ATT-0112 clause (E); they are complementary target terms, not omitted Z-terms of this datum.\n\n## 7. Descent and atlas invariance\n\nK_Z, T_Z, and phi are defined from the pair (X, Y) alone. Section 3 shows that Y is the reduced closure of an atlas-independent set of geometric points of X. Therefore any two presentations \u2014 any two smooth finite-type scheme atlases of H^bal, any \u00e9tale atlas of Hbar^bal, and the stacky incidence over H^bal itself \u2014 produce the same closed substack Y and the same datum (K_Z, T_Z, phi). Rational S_6-invariants versus coinvariants are not needed: the ordered model maps directly to the ordered stack X, and Y is formed in X.\n\n## 8. Explicitly not claimed\n\n- Tate type of T, T_Z, or K_Z; no sum of Q(8) or Q(-8) is asserted (FND-0053, FND-0152(ii), and the theorem's exclusion stand).\n- A closed embedding of Z (or of the reduced-support open of AJ) into X; Z maps to X by f_beta, which is not proper, and Y is a closure of a constructible image, not Z itself (FND-0052).\n- Gysin H^{18}(Y)(-4) -> H^{26}(X), regular immersions, lci structure, purity of codimension, or any degree shift by twice a codimension (FND-0052, FND-0068, FND-0168(5)).\n- Monomorphism, quasi-finiteness, unramifiedness, or inertia isomorphisms for f_beta; Aut(C, Gamma) is not computed (FND-0098, FND-0137). FND-0147 is not invoked.\n- T_Z = T, or that Z-supported classes span T, or that K = ker(H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6}) -> H^{16}(D)) is spanned by classes on Y (FND-0168(3)-(4)).\n- Hodge conjecture identifications of K_Z with algebraic cycle classes.\n- Any statement over nonreduced bases, with integral coefficients, or on coarse moduli.\n- Dimension of Y, equidimensionality of Y, or that dim Y = 17.\n\nThe interface is the weakest sufficient cohomological accounting that names, inside a localization sequence for M_{6,6}, the part of T supported on the atlas-independent closure of the ordered reduced-support CE geometry.",

Theorem A: the support of T_Z collapses to dimension at most 16\n\n**Theorem A.** Let Y be the reduced closed substack of X supplied by (I1) and let T_Z = ker(r_T) be the interface subquotient of (I3). Fix an admissible chain as in Lemma 1 and let j_0 be the least index with n_{j_0} <= 16 (and j_0 := N if no such index exists). Then\n\n  T_Z = ker( T -> W_{26}H^{26}( X minus Y^{(j_0)} ; Q)(21) ),  with dim Y^{(j_0)} <= 16 and Y^{(j_0)} contained in Y.\n\nIn particular, every stratum of the chain of dimension >= 17 contributes nothing to T_Z, and T_Z consists exactly of the classes in T supported on a closed reduced substack of Y of dimension at most 16, i.e. of codimension at least 5 in M_{6,6}.\n\n*Proof.* For j < j_0 we have n_j >= 17, so A_j = A_{j+1} by Lemma 3(a). So Theorem A does **not** distinguish the CE support from the ambient by codimension, and the \"codimension four\" label of the CE model plays no role in it. This is stated explicitly to avoid suggesting a separation that is not proved.\n3. **It is a vanishing from affineness plus a degree inequality, not from smallness.** The archive constraints \"Unnamed lower-dimensional strata contribute only zero or Tate classes to degree-26 cohomology with supports\" and \"Positive-codimension strata cannot contribute to the weight-26 degree-26 term solely because they have smaller dimension\" are respected: the only vanishings proved are (a) 2n-16 > n together with Artin vanishing on an affine coarse space, and (b) 2n-16 < 0. ## 0. Status of this artifact, stated first

The assigned exact theorem -- that the named C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE subquotient T_Z of T := W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8) -- is **not proved here**, and no disproof is offered either. Per FND-0189 I explicitly do **not** claim that the C66-TATE-SUPPORT artifact contract is met, and per FND-0188 I never assume RED-0001 (that T is Tate) at any point.

What is proved here, unconditionally, is a localization theorem about the *same* named T_Z:

* **Theorem A.** T_Z is the part of T supported on a closed reduced substack of Y of dimension at most 16. Equivalently: the whole dimension->=17 part of the Casnati-Ekedahl classifying-image closure -- in particular the 17-dimensional ordered reduced-support model that carries the CE geometry -- contributes nothing to T_Z.
* **Theorem B.** T_Z splits canonically as a finite direct sum of at most nine pure weight -16 pieces indexed by stratum dimension n in {8,...,16}; the n = 8 piece is automatically a finite direct sum of Q(8); the pieces for n <= 7 and n >= 17 vanish.
* **Corollary C.** If the at most eight groups W_{2n-16}H^{2n-16}(S_{(n)};Q), 9 <= n <= 16, are of Tate type Q(8-n)^{\oplus m_n}, then T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8), i.e. the assigned theorem holds.

Theorem A *derives* the upper cutoff 16 that FND-0191 clause (ii) writes down without derivation ("residual strata of dimensions 9 through 16"), and it does so without using FND-0181's dim Y <= 20 or the FND-0187 PGL_2-quotient repair dim Y <= 17: no dimension bound for Y is used at all. It is also carried out entirely inside ordinary Q-cohomology of *smooth* Deligne-Mumford stacks, so it needs no Borel-Moore or compact-support mixed Hodge formalism on the singular substack Y -- exactly the formalism FND-0165 withholds and which FND-0186 has to assume as a hypothesis.

The residual obligation is recorded as an explicit gap in Section 9.

## 1. Conventions and the imported interface datum

Work over C with Q-coefficients. Write X := M_{6,6}, the smooth separated Deligne-Mumford stack of smooth genus-six curves with six ordered marked points, of pure dimension d = 3*6-3+6 = 21 (established working-context fact). By Poincare duality (established fact; packet FND-0001)

  T := W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q) is identified with W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21),

and since X is smooth, H^{26}(X;Q) has weights >= 26, so W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q) = Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q) is a pure polarizable Hodge structure of weight 26 and T is pure polarizable of weight -16. The arithmetic ledger is 2*21-16 = 26 and 26-2*21 = -16; the Tate-twist conversion is Q(-13)(21) = Q(8) (established facts, reusable computations).

From the verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum ATT-0120, dual-confirmed by REV-0169 and REV-0170, I import exactly the following and nothing else:

* **(I1)** [ATT-0120/CLM-0120-2] There is a reduced closed substack Y of X, atlas-independent, whose underlying space is the Zariski closure of the geometric image of the classifying morphism f from the ordered reduced-support Casnati-Ekedahl model. (I use only that Y is *a reduced closed substack of X*; nothing about its dimension, purity, irreducibility, or defining equations is used.)
* **(I2)** [ATT-0120/CLM-0120-3] U_Y := X minus Y is an open substack of X, smooth of dimension 21; restriction r : H^{26}(X;Q) -> H^{26}(U_Y;Q) is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures; both sides have weights >= 26; and r_T : T -> W_{26}H^{26}(U_Y;Q)(21) is the induced morphism of pure weight -16 Hodge structures.
* **(I3)** [ATT-0120/CLM-0120-4] T_Z = K_Z := ker(r_T), a subobject of T, with phi : T_Z -> T the inclusion; degree, weight and Poincare twist are those of T.
* **(I4)** [ATT-0120/CLM-0120-5, CLM-0120-6] The coverage and atlas-invariance clauses: every class in T supported on a closed subset of X contained in Y lies in T_Z, and the datum depends only on the pair (X, Y).
* **(I5)** [ATT-0120/CLM-0120-7] The datum carries no Tate assertion and uses no Gysin map, closed embedding of Z, or support-exhaustion statement.

Nothing below re-derives, strengthens, or repairs any of (I1)-(I5); in particular I do not touch the ATT-0112 source geometry, whose artifacts are not among my dependency artifacts.

## 2. Standard inputs

These are named as standard theory, not proved here. Each is already in the register that ATT-0120/CLM-0120-3 used and that REV-0169 and REV-0170 confirmed.

* **(S1)** Deligne mixed Hodge structures on ordinary Q-cohomology of smooth separated finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks over C, functorial for open immersions; for such a stack V, H^m(V;Q) has weights >= m.
* **(S2)** *Purity / Gysin for a smooth pair.* If V is a smooth separated finite-type DM stack over C of pure dimension D and S is a **smooth** closed substack of V of **pure** codimension c, with open complement V minus S, then there is a long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures

  ... -> H^{m-2c}(S;Q)(-c) -> H^m(V;Q) -> H^m(V minus S;Q) -> H^{m-2c+1}(S;Q)(-c) -> ...

  This is purity for a closed immersion between objects **both smooth over the base**, which is precisely the route the working-context constraint on determinantal/lci reasoning itself prescribes ("The valid route is a closed immersion between schemes smooth over the base, whose codimension is the relative-dimension difference"). No regular-immersion, lci, or expected-codimension hypothesis is invoked, and this is *not* the forbidden Gysin morphism for the pair (M_{6,6}, Z) of FND-0052 / FND-0168(5a): the pairs used below are (X minus Y^{(j+1)}, S_j) with S_j smooth and closed in the smooth ambient **by construction**.
* **(S3)** *Coarse comparison for ordinary cohomology.* If S is a separated finite-type DM stack over C with coarse space c : S -> S^c, then c_*Q = Q and R^q c_* Q = 0 for q > 0, because the geometric stalks are Q-cohomology of BG for finite groups G, which vanishes in positive degrees with Q-coefficients. Hence H^*(S;Q) = H^*(S^c;Q). This is used **only** to import Artin vanishing for ordinary cohomology; no moduli-theoretic, integral, or compact-support statement on a coarse space is made, so FND-0075 and FND-0165 are not engaged.
* **(S4)** *Artin vanishing.* For an affine complex variety A of dimension n, H^k(A;Q) = 0 for k > n. (For smooth A this is Andreotti-Frankel: A has the homotopy type of a CW complex of real dimension <= n.)
* **(S5)** *Strictness.* Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for W, so W_m and Gr^W_m are exact functors on mixed Hodge structures.
* **(S6)** *Semisimplicity.* The category of pure polarizable rational Hodge structures of a fixed weight is semisimple abelian; every subobject or quotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8) is again a finite direct sum of Q(8) (established working-context fact).

## 3. Admissible chains

**Lemma 1.** Let Y be a reduced closed substack of X. There exist an integer N and reduced closed substacks

  Y = Y^{(0)} superset Y^{(1)} superset ... superset Y^{(N)} = empty

such that, writing S_j := Y^{(j)} minus Y^{(j+1)} and n_j := dim Y^{(j)}, each S_j is a locally closed substack of X which is **smooth of pure dimension n_j**, has **affine coarse space**, and is **closed in X minus Y^{(j+1)}**; moreover n_0 > n_1 > ... > n_{N-1} >= 0.

*Proof.* Recursive. Given a nonempty reduced closed substack Y^{(j)} of dimension d_j, let C_1,...,C_r be its irreducible components of dimension d_j and put

  O := Y^{(j)} minus ( union of the components of dimension < d_j, union of the pairwise intersections C_a cap C_b for a != b, union Sing(Y^{(j)}) ).

In characteristic zero the smooth locus of a reduced finite-type stack is dense open, so O is open in Y^{(j)}, smooth, of pure dimension d_j, dense in each C_a, and its connected pieces O cap C_a are pairwise disjoint. The coarse space O^c is a locally closed subscheme of the quasi-projective coarse space M_{6,6}, hence quasi-projective, and it is the disjoint union of the (O cap C_a)^c. Choose a nonempty affine open A_a in each (O cap C_a)^c and let S_j be the open substack of O lying over the affine scheme A := A_1 sqcup ... sqcup A_r (a finite disjoint union of affines is affine). Then S_j is smooth of pure dimension d_j with affine coarse space, and it is dense in each C_a.

Put Y^{(j+1)} := Y^{(j)} minus S_j with its reduced structure; it is closed in Y^{(j)}, hence in X. It is the union of the components of dimension < d_j together with the sets C_a minus S_j, each a proper closed subset of the irreducible C_a; hence dim Y^{(j+1)} <= d_j - 1 < n_j. Finally S_j = Y^{(j)} cap (X minus Y^{(j+1)}) is closed in X minus Y^{(j+1)} because Y^{(j)} is closed in X. Strict decrease of the dimensions forces termination with Y^{(N)} = empty. []

Because the n_j strictly decrease, **each integer occurs at most once** as a stratum dimension. This is what will bound the residual obligation by eight groups.

## 4. The support filtration and its graded pieces

Fix an admissible chain as in Lemma 1 and set V_j := X minus Y^{(j)}, an open substack of X, hence smooth of pure dimension 21 by (I2)-style openness. Then V_0 = U_Y, V_N = X, V_j is contained in V_{j+1}, and V_{j+1} minus S_j = V_j.

Define, for 0 <= j <= N,

  A_j := ker( T -> W_{26}H^{26}(V_j;Q)(21) ),

the map being W_{26} of the restriction H^{26}(X;Q) -> H^{26}(V_j;Q), twisted by (21). Each A_j is a subobject of T, hence pure polarizable of weight -16.

* A_0 = T_Z, by (I3) (V_0 = U_Y and the map is exactly r_T).
* A_N = 0, since V_N = X and the restriction is the identity.
* A_{j+1} is contained in A_j: restriction to V_j factors through restriction to the larger open V_{j+1}, so a class killed on V_{j+1} is killed on V_j.

**Lemma 2.** For each j, the quotient A_j / A_{j+1} is (isomorphic to) a subquotient of

  W_{2n_j-16} H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q) (n_j),

a pure polarizable Hodge structure of weight -16.

*Proof.* Apply (S2) to the smooth ambient V_{j+1} of pure dimension 21 and its smooth closed substack S_j of pure codimension c_j := 21 - n_j, at m = 26. Since m - 2c_j = 26 - 2(21-n_j) = 2n_j - 16, exactness gives

  ker( H^{26}(V_{j+1};Q) -> H^{26}(V_j;Q) ) = image( H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(-c_j) -> H^{26}(V_{j+1};Q) ).

By (S5) the functor W_{26} is exact, so it commutes with kernels and images:

  ker( W_{26}H^{26}(V_{j+1};Q) -> W_{26}H^{26}(V_j;Q) ) = W_{26} image( H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(-c_j) -> H^{26}(V_{j+1};Q) ),

and the right-hand side is a quotient of W_{26}( H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(-c_j) ).

Now consider the restriction map alpha : A_j -> W_{26}H^{26}(V_{j+1};Q)(21). Its kernel is A_j cap A_{j+1} = A_{j+1}. Its image lies in the kernel displayed above (twisted by (21)), because every class in A_j already restricts to zero on the smaller open V_j. Hence A_j / A_{j+1} embeds into that kernel, which is a quotient of W_{26}( H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(-c_j) )(21).

Finally, S_j is smooth, so by (S1) H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q) has weights >= 2n_j-16, and therefore H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(-c_j) has weights >= (2n_j-16) + 2c_j = (2n_j-16) + (42-2n_j) = 26. Consequently W_{26} of it equals W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(-c_j), the lowest-weight ("pure") piece of the cohomology of the smooth stratum, twisted. Twisting by (21) and using (-c_j) + (21) = n_j gives the stated object; its weight is (2n_j-16) - 2n_j = -16. []

## 5. Vanishing at both ends of the dimension range

**Lemma 3.** With the notation of Lemma 1 and Lemma 2:

**(a)** If n_j >= 17, then H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q) = 0 and hence A_j = A_{j+1}.

**(b)** If n_j <= 7, then H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q) = 0 and hence A_j = A_{j+1}.

**(c)** If n_j = 8, then W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j) = H^0(S_j;Q)(8), which is Q(8)^{\oplus #pi_0(S_j)}, a finite direct sum of Q(8).

*Proof.* (a) n_j >= 17 gives 2n_j - 16 = n_j + (n_j - 16) >= n_j + 1 > n_j = dim S_j. By (S3), H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q) = H^{2n_j-16}(S_j^c;Q), and S_j^c is an affine variety of dimension n_j, so this vanishes by (S4). Lemma 2 then gives A_j / A_{j+1} = 0.

Note the numerics for the only dimensions that can occur inside the 21-dimensional X: n_j = 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 give 2n_j-16 = 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, each strictly larger than n_j.

(b) n_j <= 7 gives 2n_j - 16 <= -2 < 0, and cohomology in negative degree vanishes. (Equivalently: H^{BM}_{16} of a space of dimension < 8 vanishes because 16 > 2 dim, which is the vanishing already recorded in FND-0186.)

(c) n_j = 8 gives 2n_j - 16 = 0, and H^0(S_j;Q) = Q^{#pi_0(S_j)} is pure of weight 0, so W_0H^0 = H^0. Twisting by (8) gives Q(8)^{\oplus #pi_0(S_j)}. []

## 6. Theorem A: the support of T_Z collapses to dimension at most 16

**Theorem A.** Let Y be the reduced closed substack of X supplied by (I1) and let T_Z = ker(r_T) be the interface subquotient of (I3). Fix an admissible chain as in Lemma 1 and let j_0 be the least index with n_{j_0} <= 16 (and j_0 := N if no such index exists). Then

  T_Z = ker( T -> W_{26}H^{26}( X minus Y^{(j_0)} ; Q)(21) ),  with dim Y^{(j_0)} <= 16 and Y^{(j_0)} contained in Y.

In particular, every stratum of the chain of dimension >= 17 contributes nothing to T_Z, and T_Z consists exactly of the classes in T supported on a closed reduced substack of Y of dimension at most 16, i.e. of codimension at least 5 in M_{6,6}.

*Proof.* For j < j_0 we have n_j >= 17, so A_j = A_{j+1} by Lemma 3(a). Hence T_Z = A_0 = A_{j_0}, which is the displayed kernel; and n_{j_0} = dim Y^{(j_0)} <= 16 by the definition of j_0 (if j_0 = N then Y^{(N)} = empty and T_Z = 0, which is the empty direct sum of Q(8) and is consistent with the statement). []

Three remarks on the scope of Theorem A, stated so that it is not overread.

1. **No dimension input for Y is used.** The proof only ever needs dim Y <= dim X = 21, which is automatic for a closed substack. FND-0181's dim Y <= 20 and FND-0186/FND-0187's repaired dim Y <= 17 are consistent with Theorem A but are not used; in particular Theorem A does not depend on the FND-0187 PGL_2-quotient repair, and it does not assert dim Y = 17 or dim Y = 20 (which FND-0181 lists as not covered).
2. **Theorem A is a general principle, not a separation of T_Z from T.** The same argument applied with Y = X shows that T itself is the part of T supported on a closed substack of dimension at most 16. So Theorem A does **not** distinguish the CE support from the ambient by codimension, and the "codimension four" label of the CE model plays no role in it. This is stated explicitly to avoid suggesting a separation that is not proved.
3. **It is a vanishing from affineness plus a degree inequality, not from smallness.** The archive constraints "Unnamed lower-dimensional strata contribute only zero or Tate classes to degree-26 cohomology with supports" and "Positive-codimension strata cannot contribute to the weight-26 degree-26 term solely because they have smaller dimension" are respected: the only vanishings proved are (a) 2n-16 > n together with Artin vanishing on an affine coarse space, and (b) 2n-16 < 0. Neither is an inference from smallness of the stratum, and Theorem B below leaves the intermediate dimensions entirely undetermined rather than declaring them zero or Tate.

## 7. Theorem B: canonical splitting into at most nine pieces

**Theorem B.** With the notation above, T_Z carries the finite decreasing filtration T_Z = A_{j_0} superset A_{j_0+1} superset ... superset A_N = 0 by sub-Hodge structures, and

  T_Z is isomorphic to the direct sum over j_0 <= j < N of A_j / A_{j+1},

where for each j the piece A_j / A_{j+1} is a subquotient of W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j). Moreover:

* A_j / A_{j+1} = 0 whenever n_j <= 7 or n_j >= 17;
* A_j / A_{j+1} is a finite direct sum of Q(8) whenever n_j = 8;
* the remaining pieces are indexed by the dimensions n_j in {9,10,...,16}, and since the n_j strictly decrease there are **at most eight** of them, at most one for each such dimension.

*Proof.* The filtration and the identification of its graded pieces are Lemma 2. Every A_j is a subobject of the pure polarizable weight -16 structure T, hence is itself pure polarizable of weight -16; so are all the graded pieces. By (S6) the category of pure polarizable weight -16 rational Hodge structures is semisimple, so the finite filtration splits and T_Z is the direct sum of its graded pieces. The three bullet points are Lemma 3(a), 3(b), 3(c) together with (S6) (a subquotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8) is a finite direct sum of Q(8)). Strict decrease of the n_j gives the count. []

**Corollary C (sufficient criterion for the assigned theorem).** Suppose that for one admissible chain, and for every j with 9 <= n_j <= 16, the pure weight-(2n_j-16) Hodge structure W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8-n_j). Then T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8), i.e. the assigned theorem holds.

*Proof.* The twist Q(8-n)(n) = Q(8) has weight -16, matching. Under the hypothesis every graded piece in Theorem B is a subquotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8); by (S6) each is a finite direct sum of Q(8), hence so is their direct sum T_Z. []

## 8. Consistency checks, sharpness, and what a disproof must now do

**Check against FND-0191.** FND-0191 exhibits X' = A x P^{12} with A a complex abelian variety of dimension 9, Y' = A x {pt} of dimension 9 and codimension 12, and shows that the image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y';Q) in W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X';Q) is H^2(A)(9), pure polarizable of weight -16 with Hodge types (-7,-9), (-8,-8), (-9,-7) and hence not a finite direct sum of Q(8). Theorem B reproduces this exactly: the chain has the single stratum S_0 = Y' of dimension n_0 = 9, and its graded piece is W_{2*9-16}H^{2}(A;Q)(9) = H^2(A)(9), since A is proper so H^2(A;Q) is already pure of weight 2. So Theorem B is sharp enough to see the adjudicated counterexample, and dimension 9 -- inside the residual range -- is where it sits.

**Check against FND-0169.** FND-0169 locates a non-Tate class of Hodge type (15,1) in Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(V;Q) for a 15-dimensional etale atlas V of Hbar^bal. In the dictionary of Theorem B a stratum of dimension n = 15 contributes W_{14}H^{14}(S;Q)(15), whose Hodge types are (a-15, b-15) with a+b = 14; the choice (a,b) = (0,14) gives type (-15,-1), the dual of (15,1). So that recorded hazard also lies strictly inside the residual range 9 <= n <= 16 and is **not** removed by Theorem A. I make no claim that this class is on Y or that its image in T is nonzero; FND-0178 records that such witnesses do not address the target.

**Sharpness of the cutoff 16.** The cutoff cannot be pushed below 16 by the present method: for a stratum S smooth affine of dimension n <= 16 the degree 2n-16 satisfies 2n-16 <= n, so (S4) gives no vanishing, and already for n = 1 the lowest-weight piece W_1H^1(S;Q) of an affine curve is H^1 of its smooth compactification, which is nonzero and non-Tate in general. So Artin vanishing genuinely stops at 17.

**What a disproof must now do.** By Theorem A, a class living only on the dimension->=17 part of Y -- in particular on the 17-dimensional ordered reduced-support Casnati-Ekedahl model itself, which is where the packet's non-Tate hazards for the CE geometry are usually located -- restricts to zero in this accounting and therefore cannot exhibit a non-Tate subquotient of T_Z. Combined with the theorem's own exclusion clause, a disproof must now (i) produce a non-Tate class in W_{2n-16}H^{2n-16}(S;Q)(n) for a stratum S of Y of dimension 9 <= n <= 16, and (ii) prove that its image in T is nonzero. Neither is attempted here, and non-Tate cohomology of a family base, atlas, product model, or standalone Z remains, per the theorem statement, not a disproof.

## 9. The gap, and blocked routes not walked

**GAP-C66-TATE-STRATA-9-16.** For 9 <= n <= 16, the pure Hodge structure W_{2n-16}H^{2n-16}(S_{(n)};Q) of the dimension-n stratum of an admissible chain for Y is not determined by anything proved here. This is the recorded frontier obligation on the mixed Hodge structure of the Casnati-Ekedahl ordering-cover geometry ("The H_alpha-object given by ordinary or Borel-Moore cohomology of a connected component of the ordering cover, as a mixed Hodge structure; the induction isomorphism does not determine Tate type of that object"), now localized to at most eight groups. It is **not discharged**. Consequently the assigned theorem is not established by this artifact, and Corollary C is a proved implication whose antecedent is open; per FND-0189 I do not present it as meeting the C66-TATE-SUPPORT contract.

**Blocked routes and recorded constraints, explicitly not walked.**

* *vcd-only-vanishing*: neither vcd(M_{6,6}) = 26 nor vcd(M_{6,5}) = 25 appears anywhere in the argument. Artin vanishing (S4) is applied only to affine coarse spaces of strata of Y, never to M_{6,6}, never to the target degree, and it yields vanishing of an auxiliary cohomology group, not of the target.
* *undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex*: never used; Mbar_{6,6}, its boundary, and top-weight graph complexes never appear.
* *point-count-without-degree-parity-separation*: no point count, no finite computation of any kind is used.
* *forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown*: the forgetful map M_{6,6} -> M_{6,5} is never used, and T is never renamed as cohomology with local-system coefficients.
* FND-0052 / FND-0168(5a),(5b): no closed embedding of the balanced reduced-support model into M_{6,6}, no pure-codimension-four closed substack, no Gysin map for the pair (M_{6,6}, Z), and no degree shift by twice a codimension of Z. Every purity sequence used is (S2) for a pair of smooth objects constructed in Lemma 1.
* Working-context constraint on expected determinantal codimension implying lci/regular immersion: not used; I use exactly the alternative that constraint itself prescribes, a closed immersion between smooth objects with codimension equal to the dimension difference.
* FND-0053, FND-0085, FND-0054: no Tate conclusion is drawn from rationality of the irreducible representations of S_6, from a finite branch morphism of the Hurwitz stack to an open of a moduli of pointed rational curves, or from declaring the Hurwitz space rational/Tate. No cohomology of H, H^bal, Hbar^bal, or the ordering cover is computed or assumed anywhere.
* FND-0165: no compact-support or Borel-Moore mixed Hodge formalism on the singular substack Y is used; the whole argument runs in ordinary Q-cohomology of smooth DM stacks. (FND-0186 by contrast has to assume coarse-space agreement for H_c of the relevant stacks; I need only the ordinary-cohomology comparison (S3).)
* FND-0188: RED-0001 is never assumed; T is never asserted to be Tate, and no step uses Tate-ness of T.
* FND-0168(3),(4): no support-exhaustion T_Z = T is claimed, no equivalence between Tate type and spanning by algebraic cycle classes is asserted, and the Hodge conjecture is not used.
* FND-0181/FND-0187: no dimension bound for Y is used and no equality dim Y = 17 or 20 is asserted.
* Archive constraint "An open subset of an affine stack is automatically affine": not used. Affineness of each S_j is *constructed* in Lemma 1 by choosing an affine open of a quasi-projective coarse space, not inferred from affineness of an ambient.

**Not claimed.** Tate type of T_Z or of T; nonvanishing of T_Z; support-exhaustion; any statement about unbalanced Casnati-Ekedahl strata or whether they lie in Y; any assembly of complementary target terms; anything with integral coefficients, over nonreduced bases, or of moduli-theoretic content on coarse spaces.

claims.statement: For any reduced closed substack Y of X = M_{6,6} there is a finite chain Y = Y^{(0)} superset ... superset Y^{(N)} = empty of reduced closed substacks whose successive differences S_j = Y^{(j)} minus Y^{(j+1)} are smooth of pure dimension n_j = dim Y^{(j)}, have affine coarse space, are closed in X minus Y^{(j+1)}, and satisfy n_0 > n_1 > ... > n_{N-1} >= 0. No dimension bound for Y is needed.

With A_j := ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus Y^{(j)};Q)(21)), one has A_0 = T_Z (the ATT-0120/CLM-0120-4 datum), A_N = 0, and A_{j+1} contained in A_j; and for each j the graded piece A_j/A_{j+1} is a subquotient of the pure weight -16 Hodge structure W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j). The proof uses only the purity sequence for the smooth pair (X minus Y^{(j+1)}, S_j), exactness of W_{26}, and the weight bound for smooth stacks; no Gysin map for (M_{6,6},Z), no closed embedding of Z, and no lci or codimension-purity hypothesis is used.

If n_j >= 17 then H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q) = 0, because 2n_j-16 > n_j = dim S_j and S_j has affine coarse space (Artin/Andreotti-Frankel vanishing via the coarse comparison for ordinary Q-cohomology); consequently A_j = A_{j+1}. If n_j <= 7 then 2n_j-16 < 0 and again A_j = A_{j+1}. If n_j = 8 then the graded piece is a subquotient of H^0(S_j;Q)(8) = Q(8)^{\oplus #pi_0(S_j)}, hence a finite direct sum of Q(8).

Theorem A: T_Z = ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus Y^{(j_0)};Q)(21)) where Y^{(j_0)} is a closed reduced substack of Y of dimension at most 16. Equivalently, the entire dimension->=17 part of the Casnati-Ekedahl classifying-image closure, including the 17-dimensional ordered reduced-support model, contributes nothing to T_Z, and T_Z is the part of T supported in codimension at least 5. This derives the upper cutoff 16 that FND-0191 clause (ii) states without derivation, and it uses neither FND-0181's dim Y <= 20 nor FND-0187's repaired dim Y <= 17.

Theorem B: T_Z is isomorphic to the direct sum of the graded pieces A_j/A_{j+1}, each a subquotient of W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j); the pieces with n_j <= 7 or n_j >= 17 vanish, the piece with n_j = 8 is a finite direct sum of Q(8), and the remaining pieces are indexed by dimensions in {9,...,16}, at most one per dimension, hence at most eight of them. The splitting uses semisimplicity of pure polarizable weight -16 rational Hodge structures.

Corollary C: if for one admissible chain and every j with 9 <= n_j <= 16 the group W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8-n_j), then T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8). This is a proved implication; its antecedent is the open gap GAP-C66-TATE-STRATA-9-16 and is not established here, so the assigned theorem is not discharged by this artifact.

Consistency: the FND-0191 model X' = A x P^{12}, Y' = A x {pt} with dim A = 9 is reproduced exactly by Theorem B as the single stratum of dimension 9 with graded piece H^2(A)(9), non-Tate; and the FND-0169 Hodge type (15,1) corresponds to a dimension-15 stratum contributing type (-15,-1). Both lie inside the residual range 9 <= n <= 16, so Theorem A removes neither, and no claim is made that either class lies on Y or has nonzero image in T.

parsed_artifact.summary: This artifact does NOT prove the assigned theorem; it proves an unconditional localization theorem that strictly narrows the residual obligation, and it records the remainder as an explicit gap. Work over C with Q-coefficients on X = M_{6,6} (smooth DM stack, dim 21), with T = W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q) = W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21) and with the dual-confirmed C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum of ATT-0120 (REV-0169, REV-0170): Y the reduced closed classifying-image closure, T_Z = ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus Y;Q)(21)), phi the inclusion. Choose an admissible chain Y = Y^{(0)} superset ... superset Y^{(N)} = empty whose successive differences S_j are smooth of pure dimension n_j = dim Y^{(j)} with affine coarse space; then n_0 > n_1 > ... . Purity for the smooth pair (X minus Y^{(j+1)}, S_j) turns the j-th step of the induced filtration A_j = ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus Y^{(j)};Q)(21)) into a subquotient of W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j). Two vanishings follow: for n_j >= 17 one has 2n_j-16 > n_j, so Artin vanishing on the affine coarse space kills the term (Theorem A), and for n_j <= 7 the degree 2n_j-16 is negative. Hence T_Z equals the part of T supported on a closed substack of Y of dimension at most 16 -- the entire dimension->=17 part of the CE support, including the 17-dimensional ordered reduced-support model itself, contributes nothing. By semisimplicity of pure polarizable weight -16 Hodge structures, T_Z splits as a direct sum of at most nine pieces, one for each stratum dimension n in {8,...,16}; the n=8 piece is automatically a finite direct sum of Q(8) (it is a subquotient of H^0(S;Q)(8)). This derives, rather than stipulates, the upper cutoff 16 written in FND-0191(ii), and it does so without FND-0181's dim Y <= 20 or FND-0187's PGL_2-quotient repair dim Y <= 17, and without any Borel-Moore/compact-support formalism on the singular Y (FND-0165). The residual obligation -- Tate type of the at most eight groups W_{2n-16}H^{2n-16}(S_{(n)};Q) for 9 <= n <= 16 -- is recorded as GAP-C66-TATE-STRATA-9-16 and is not discharged; RED-0001 is never assumed (FND-0188), and no claim is made that the C66-TATE-SUPPORT contract of FND-0189 is met.
